power.capacity-scope: the load the PDU can hand on, 11 kW (the "Output kW" column of the maker's table). It is not what the PDU draws itself, which the basic version does not state

configs.description: The PDU as it ships: the fixed cord and the two push-button attachments on it. The universal mounting kit, the connector lock and the mounting adaptor are not drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the data sheet says black anodised RAL 9005 ("other colours may be configured"); both photographs show a natural silver extrusion. Silver is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a rating plate or order note naming the finish of this SKU.

gaps.note: the table prints 1095 and the drawing dimensions 1094. The drawing is used because every position is read off it.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on which is the tolerance.

gaps.note: the circuit diagram numbers 29 positions for 27 outlets and the photograph prints none; no name is taken, so the placement ids stand.
gaps.wanted: a drawing or photograph of the printed outlet numbers.

gaps.note: the phase groups are drawn as full-width plates in the colours of the render (the data sheet: L1 pink, L2 black, L3 white); the render shows a narrow silver margin at each edge that no source measures, and its pink reads red.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front with a scale.

gaps.note: the mounting adaptor 7000.688 and the universal mounting kit are named and not drawn; the attachment on the enclosure frame at the side of the 19" frame is named and not dimensioned.
the end view draws the strip's section with the gland and the button and no detail; no photograph looks at an end or a side straight on.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of an end and a side.

gaps.note: this 16 A SKU has no breaker (the data sheet: breakers only in 32 A versions), so no outlet states `through`.

gaps.wanted: one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `power` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

breakers.note: datasheet - dri1308088en p.1: "No. of circuit-breakers 2 (single-phase) or 6 (3-phase) with 32 A version"; the table prints this SKU at 16 A and the sheet's feature table has the breaker "only for 32 A PDU versions", so a 16 A version has none. No breaker is drawn and none is stated.

chassis.note: drawing - length 1094 (the table of page 1 of the PDU basic sheet prints 1095; see gaps: length), width 44 (the data sheet's "44 mm (1 U)"), depth 72.1 (the side view's dimension, the body from the front face to the back). THE DEPTH DISAGREEMENT: the data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) prints "PDU enclosure depth 70 mm", the side view 72.1 and the end view 109. The end view's 109 is the 72.1 body together with the cable gland standing out of the front and the button standing out of the back (the end view draws both), so 109 is the envelope and not the body; the 70 mm is the extrusion profile (1 U x 70 mm, page 3 of the same sheet), which the drawing's 72.1 exceeds by the 2.1 of face moulding and cover. 72.1 is drawn. The 144 of the 19" variants is a different SKU.

colour.note: THE DATA SHEET AND THE PHOTOGRAPHS DISAGREE. The data sheet (dri1308088en, p.1) says "Aluminium, anodised in RAL 9005 (black, other colours may be configured)"; both photographs held show a natural silver side. The body is drawn silver as photographed (#b9bbbe, read by eye, estimated) and the disagreement is a gap.

dcim.note: the input is one power port from the cord part and each outlet a power outlet it feeds. C13 and C19 export as the IEC types; the earthing-pin socket and the CEE plug export as `other` with a label, because no upstream type for either has been read from a held source.

front.note: drawing - the front view of page 25, mm from the foot end: the gland in the foot cell (centre 36.1, on the width); in each group the six C13 on a 28.4 pitch from 10.0 after the block's start (read as the cell lines of the zoomed render), the C19 cell, and two earthing-pin sockets. ORIENTATION, read off the front view and turned with the strip standing on its foot: the C13 long axis lies across the strip with the earth side toward the head; the C19 long axis lies along the strip with its earth slot toward the left of the face; the sockets' contact holes sit on one diagonal. Outlets count from the foot.

input.note: datasheet - dri1308088en p.1: "Input voltage range (L - N) 230 V (400 V, 3~), 50 - 60 Hz", "Input current 16 A/32 A (depending on product variant)", "No. of wires 3/5", "Connection cable type H05-VV", "Length of connection cable 3m"; the table: 3~, 16 A, 11 kW, input CEE. The circuit diagram draws the neutral to each phase group (CEE 16 A/3P + N + PE), so each outlet is line to neutral: `input-wiring: wye`. The unit has a fixed cord and no inlet. `plug-rating-a` is not written: the data sheet rates the unit, not the plug.

lifecycle.note: the maker's page lists the SKU among the 27 basic variants; no end-of-life notice was found in the pages read.

logo.note: the photograph shows a RITTAL mark on the head cap; it is not drawn: the area is the `logo-zone` region, read off the photograph.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S DIMENSIONED DRAWING. Rittal, "Technical details, Power Distribution Unit, Basic version" (dri2108028en, 08.2023), PDF page 25, DK 7979.175: a plan view (the back), a side view, an end view and a front view, with the circuit diagram below. Positions were read off 600 and 1200 dpi renders of that page. The scale is the drawing's own: the 1094 overall length between the two ends of the front view reads 2121 px at 600 dpi (1.9388 px per mm) and the 44 mm width of the strip reads 86 px (44.4); the 933.45 between the two buttons is dimensioned on the plan view. The outlet cells were read as the full-height lines of the front view: the foot cell 72.2 long, then in each group a C13 block 181.3, a C19 cell 45.65, two socket cells 44.4 and a spacer 24.2, and the head cap 26.3. Good to about 0.5 mm. The photograph (Rittal render of the same SKU, one near-elevation) is the second reading, for the order of the cells, the colours and the logo.

mount.note: `rack-side`, the library's way to say a part stands vertically beside an upright, on the two push-button attachments of the plan view (dimensioned 933.45 apart). The data sheet's "PDU mounting options" are the enclosure frame at the side of the 482.6 mm mounting frame (zero-U space) and the cable route (push-button attachment); the mounting adaptor 7000.688 is an accessory and is not drawn. `ru: 25` is the 1094 mm it runs, 1094 / 44.45 = 24.6; the data sheet sells it by minimum rack height (1200 for a VX IT frame) and not by rack units.

mounting-buttons.note: drawing - the plan view of page 25: two buttons, the first 80.0 from the foot end, 933.45 to the second; plate 36.6 across and 25.2 along; the side view draws them standing about 7.7 out of the back.

numbering.note: the circuit diagram numbers the outlets 1 to 9 on L1, 10 to 19 on L2 and 20 to 29 on L3 with the last C13 of L2 and L3 numbered 16 and 26; 27 outlets cannot carry 29 numbers, and the photograph prints none. No name is taken.

outlets.note: datasheet and drawing - the table of page 1 ("PDU basic"): DK 7979.175, 3~, 16 A, 11 kW, CEE input, 18 IEC C13, 3 IEC C19, 6 earthing-pin, 1095 mm; the circuit diagram draws 6 x C13, 1 x C19 and 2 x CEE 7 on each of L1, L2 and L3. std/c13-outlet@1, std/c19-outlet@1 and rittal/cee-7-3-outlet@1. None is switched; none has a lamp. NO OUTLET NAME IS WRITTEN: the unit prints no numbers on the photograph and the circuit diagram's numbers (1 to 9, 10 to 19, 20 to 29) count 29 for 27 outlets (gaps: numbering), so the outlets keep their placement ids, counted from the foot.

rear.note: drawing - the plan view draws two long grooves, 12.4 to 15.0 and 30.4 to 33.0 from the left edge as seen from behind, a ridge on the centre line at 22.2 and the two buttons. The grooves are read from the first 120 mm of the strip at 600 dpi and drawn to 2.6 short of each end; the other end was not looked at.
